messages:
Elena (Support): customer ACME reports a subtle brevity/regression after the v8.2 rollout. They say answers are much shorter and lose explanatory steps. Copied their repro below (they pasted whole responses).

Customer (copied):
```prompt
Explain OAuth token rotation for an internal service used by microservices.
```

Before (redwood-v8):
```
1) Identify where tokens are stored (env/vault).
2) Create a new token with limited scope and short TTL.
3) Deploy a rolling update that loads the new token.
4) Validate by calling the health endpoint and rotating back if errors.
Example curl and code snippets provided.
Detailed rationale about revocation windows and gradual rollout.
```
After (redwood-v8.2):
```
Rotate token by calling /rotate. Ensure new token is used.
```

Elena (Support): the customer says this started right after the canary hit 100% (~2025-11-12T00:30Z). They ran with same request params across both runs. No 5xxs or latency changes on their end. They provided two request IDs: `req_8a7c9f2b` and `req_8a9d21fc` with full response bodies.

Matt (Eng-ML): can you paste the exact request payload and model params (model, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, system prompt)? :eyes:

Elena (Support): pasted their sanitized curl (they removed PII):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" \
 -d '{"model":"redwood-v8.2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a concise assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Explain OAuth token rotation for an internal service."}],"temperature":0.0,"max_tokens":300}'
```

Priya (Eng-ML): interesting — temp=0.0 and max_tokens=300, system prompt says "concise" which might bias brevity, but you said behavior changed across versions with the same prompt? any difference in system prompt text between runs?

Elena (Support): they confirmed the system prompt string was identical when they compared. They also re-ran with model set to `redwood-v8` and got the long answer again.

Sasha (SRE): infra-wise we had no GPU OOMs or kernel crashes in that window. No throttling, no queue spikes. support-bot: Canary rollout to redwood-v8.2 completed 2025-11-12T00:30Z; previous canary was redwood-v8.

Matt (Eng-ML): possible causes: 1) a behavioral change from a model refactor or distillation step in v8.2, 2) decoding/default stop-token heuristics changed, or 3) an inadvertent change in the system-level safety/conciseness objective. We need side-by-side logits/stop-token probs to be sure.

Elena (Support): customer already gave full responses but not logits. They've asked us to avoid sharing raw logs externally, but they consent to us analyzing request/response bodies and metadata internally.

Matt (Eng-ML): next steps: (a) ask for a minimal reproducible curl with headers (they already provided one), (b) request permission to run the same prompt against staging and compare logits and token-by-token outputs, (c) open model-oncall ticket and attach examples. I'll draft the ticket.

Priya (Eng-ML): hypothesis note: compare `p(stop_token)` distribution and token entropy between v8 and v8.2. Also check for changes in constrained-decoding/nav tokens, and any change to default `stop` handling. If we see a sharp rise in early stop prob, that's likely the culprit.

Elena (Support): created ticket SUP-1423 and attached the two example responses and the customer's curl. Pinging @Matt @Priya for triage. Also asked the customer if we can run internal repros using their prompt; they said yes for diagnostics only.

Sasha (SRE): leaving a note: no rollback planned yet. If model-oncall confirms behavioral regression and it's high impact across customers, ops can coordinate a temporary rollback. :thumbsup:

Matt (Eng-ML): I'll run token-level diffs on staging tonight and post results in the ticket. If anyone else sees similar noise in logs, please drop the request ids. Thanks.

Elena (Support): I'll follow up with the customer with the ticket number and ETA. Closing loop once eng posts findings. :wave:
